title: Getting Started: Your First 10 Minutes with CloudDash
content:
Welcome to CloudDash! This guide will walk you through the essential steps to get value out of the platform in under 10 minutes.

## Step 1: Connect Your First Cloud Provider

CloudDash needs data to be useful. Let's connect AWS as your first integration.

1. From the welcome screen, click **Connect Cloud Provider**.
2. Select **AWS**.
3. CloudDash will provide an AWS CloudFormation template link.
4. Click the link to open the AWS Console in a new tab. It will pre-populate a stack that creates a read-only IAM Role.
5. Check the acknowledgment box at the bottom of the AWS page and click **Create Stack**.
6. Wait ~2 minutes for the stack to complete, then copy the output **Role ARN**.
7. Paste the ARN back into CloudDash and click **Connect**.

Within 60 seconds, CloudDash will begin ingesting your AWS metrics.

## Step 2: Explore the Auto-Generated Dashboard

Once data flows in, CloudDash automatically generates a "Cloud Overview" dashboard based on the resources discovered in your account.

1. Click **Dashboards** in the left navigation menu.
2. Select **AWS Overview**.
3. You will immediately see widgets for EC2 CPU utilization, RDS database connections, and S3 bucket sizes.
4. Try changing the time range in the top right (e.g., from 'Last 1 hour' to 'Last 24 hours').

## Step 3: Create Your First Alert

Let's ensure you know when a critical instance is under heavy load.

1. Navigate to **Alerts** in the left menu.
2. Click **Create Alert**.
3. Name it: "High CPU - Production Database".
4. Select the metric: `AWS/RDS` -> `CPUUtilization`.
5. Set the condition: **Greater than 85%** for **5 minutes**.
6. Add a notification channel. By default, your email address is available. Select it.
7. Click **Save Alert**.

## Step 4: Invite Your Team

Monitoring is a team sport. Invite a colleague to share the visibility.

1. Go to **Settings → Team & Permissions**.
2. Click **Invite Member**.
3. Enter their email address and assign them the **Editor** role.
4. Click **Send Invitation**.

## Next Steps

You're all set! As a next step, consider setting up a PagerDuty or Slack integration (see kb-020) so your alerts go directly to your incident response tools rather than just your email inbox.
